body.statement: Fix \(w\ge0\). For every \(2\le p<q\) and same-transitive-closure pair of DAGs \((G,G')\) on \(V\), written in their common topological order, with \(\omega_p(G,G')\le w\), the compiler \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\) is sound and complete for deciding \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) on every full-dimensional chamber of \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). Its acceptance certificate is a finite tree of rational univariate representations and Thom signs whose projected cells form a relatively dense positive-real realization cover; its rejection certificate is a terminal-linkage, affine-support, covariance-cone-face, or strict-positivity separator with bagwise subresultant verification. If \(B=|\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')|_{\mathrm{bit}}\), the algorithm uses at most \(\widetilde O\!\left(q(B+q+1)^{2^{w+3}}\right)\) bit operations and every certificate coefficient has bit length at most \((B+q+1)^{2^{w+2}}\). The proof uses only local sign determination on width-\(w\) bags and branch gluing. If the undirected union of \(G\) and \(G'\) has pathwidth at most \(w\) and both DAGs have maximum indegree at most \(w\), then \(\omega_p(G,G')\le p(p+1)/2+(w+1)(w+2)\); hence bounded-pathwidth, bounded-indegree pairs, including directed chains and bounded-width polytrees, form an explicit infinite tractable family. The theorem-specific locus excludes \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\), covers both adjacent sign chambers, admits variance-neutral candidate twins, and makes no pointwise claim on excluded true hyperplanes.
body.justification: This theorem supplies the required tractable family and converts the fork's local sign analysis into a graph-controlled exact compiler before any all-graph claim.
body.gap: Foygel Barber et al. study half-trek criteria for identifiability of latent-variable models, while Sections IV--V of Kela et al. provide semidefinite tests and positive-semidefinite decomposition and realization machinery for latent causal structures. Wu et al. accelerate general existential Fourier--Motzkin elimination and cylindrical algebraic decomposition by tree dynamic programming over the primal graph of variables co-occurring in atomic constraints. Covariance-terminal width instead counts a domain-specific active latent frontier and one \(p(p+1)/2\)-dimensional moment state; neither width is known to dominate the other without a quantitative translation theorem. The output distinction is a dense positive-real realization cover or full-dimensional graph-frontier separator, not a claimed improvement over the complexity frontier of general quantifier elimination.
body.consumer: For bounded-width gene-regulatory and measurement graphs, the LCD workflow obtains a terminating exact certificate instead of an unrestricted semialgebraic oracle.
